title: Chapter 92 — Pipeline, Relationship, and Money Metrics
intro: Pipeline health, base and referral metrics, the income ledger, and forecasting your own business.

sections.title: Pipeline Health
sections.content:
Your pipeline is every open opportunity — every quote, every follow-up due, every customer who left without buying but gave you their information.

A healthy pipeline has volume and velocity. Volume means enough opportunities to hit your targets. Velocity means opportunities are moving forward, not sitting stale.

Review your pipeline weekly. How many open quotes? How old are they? Which ones need a follow-up call today? Which ones are dead and should be closed out?

sections.title: Relationship Metrics
sections.content:
Beyond pipeline, track your relationship health. How many past customers have you contacted this month? How many referrals came in? How many repeat customers bought from you this quarter?

These numbers tell you whether your delivered base is working for you or sitting dormant. A growing referral count means your reputation is compounding. A shrinking one means relationships are fading.

sections.title: Your Income Ledger
sections.content:
The best salespeople know their numbers the way a business owner knows theirs. What did you earn this month? What is your average ticket? What is your average commission per sale? How many sales do you need next month to hit your goal?

This is not about obsessing over money. It is about understanding the math of your career. When you know the math, you can make better decisions about where to invest your time.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating pipeline and financial awareness, ask:

Does the salesperson know their pipeline status — or is it a mystery?
Do they track relationship metrics — referrals, repeat customers, base contacts?
Do they understand the financial math of their career?
Are they forecasting — or just hoping?
